items.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
items.q: The mention of 'Clare' occurs entirely within the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn ('...it's Clare that same, the fine Clare that same woman on the music box.'). The interviewee does not respond to or acknowledge this specific mention, nor does the interviewee mention Clare in their own turns.

ctx.x: Yeah, because my brother would have been a famous musician anyway. Yes, he must have. He was a wonderful trumpet musician. He was famous when he was in the middle. He was famous. If he could hold a note, you're talking about Louis Armstrong holding a note. But little George could hold that note. And I'm sure he would have been real famous. He was only 32 when he died.

Only 32. Yes. He used to play with Henry Jr. or I said, but it's Clare that same, the fine Clare that same woman on the music box. But George was playing that legit dance on Crandelet and Canal. Right on that call. Yeah, he played seven years. He cut a record. He was working every day when he was playing a really bad night.

Well, George cut an old-time record. Millen Boy George. Yeah, yeah, he did. Oh, did he make some records? Yes, he made Millen Boy George. That's your record. Uh-huh, uh-huh. My sister was telling me about that yesterday.
